title: Audit logs: include authz decision context (policy_version, role_ids, decision_reason)
author: Kevin Osei
release_notes: Audit log events emitted by control plane now optionally include authorization decision context: authz_policy_version, authz_role_ids, authz_decision_reason. No behavior change for authorization; fields are additive and backward compatible.
commits: auditlog: add authz decision context fields to event envelope
auditlog: wire authz context from middleware into audit emitter
schemas: bump audit event schema minor version + update validation fixtures
tests: add golden tests for allow/deny events w/ authz context
docs: add field descriptions + examples for SIEM consumers
description: Summary: This PR adds authorization-decision context fields to Redwood control-plane audit log events to support RBAC v2 auditability and enterprise security reviews. Specifically we add optional fields authz_policy_version, authz_role_ids, and authz_decision_reason to the audit event envelope, and wire them from the new RBAC v2 evaluation path (middleware) into the audit emitter. Motivation: Today we can say that an action occurred and who did it, but we cannot reliably answer “why was this allowed/denied?” during audits or customer investigations. RBAC v2 requires explainable decisions, plus stable evidence for SOC 2 / ISO mapping. Scope: Control-plane audit event envelope + schema updates + tests. No changes to authorization behavior. No changes to exporter in this repo (handled separately). Fields added (all optional / additive): (1) authz_policy_version: string. The active policy bundle version used for evaluation (e.g., rbac-bundle@0.1.3). (2) authz_role_ids: array of strings. Role IDs present on the actor at time of decision (UUIDs; do not log display names). (3) authz_decision_reason: string enum-ish code. A stable machine-readable reason code for allow/deny (examples below). Semantics: We only emit authz context for events that correspond to an authorization check. For events not gated by RBAC (legacy paths, system-only events), fields remain absent. For multi-check flows, we attach the decision that gated the audited action (not intermediate preflight checks). Reason codes (initial set): ALLOW, DENY_MISSING_PERMISSION, DENY_SCOPE_MISMATCH, DENY_POLICY_NOT_LOADED, DENY_EXPLICITLY_DISABLED, DENY_IMPERSONATION_NOT_ALLOWED, DENY_BREAK_GLASS_REQUIRED. Notes: (a) We intentionally do NOT log evaluated policy statements, resource attributes, or raw permission sets to avoid log bloat and leaking sensitive internal policy structure. (b) role_ids are IDs only; any mapping to human-readable names occurs in the console using org state, not in logs. (c) policy_version is the bundle version string returned by the policy cache; when unavailable we set decision_reason=DENY_POLICY_NOT_LOADED for deny paths and omit policy_version. Schema changes: audit_event.schema.json minor bump; new fields are optional and default-omitted. Added fixtures for allow and deny examples. Example emitted audit event snippet: "authz_policy_version":"rbac-bundle@0.1.3","authz_role_ids":["role_9f2c...","role_1b7a..."],"authz_decision_reason":"DENY_MISSING_PERMISSION". Testing: Added golden tests covering allow and deny flows from the authz middleware into the audit emitter; schema validation fixtures updated; ensured existing fixtures continue to validate without new fields present. Rollout / compatibility: Backward compatible. Consumers that don’t recognize these fields should ignore them. Exporter updates are tracked in audit-log-exporter PR #88; policy-bundle version strings align with rbac-policy-bundle v0.1 line. Follow-ups: (1) ensure all high-risk endpoints emit audit events with authz context (inventory work in ENG-5381/ENG-5387); (2) add dashboards/alerts for DENY_POLICY_NOT_LOADED spikes to detect policy distribution issues; (3) update external customer-facing audit log field reference once RBAC v2 exits beta.
conversation: Marcus Lin (review): Can we make sure decision_reason values are stable and documented? Also please confirm we’re not leaking policy contents or permission lists.

Kevin Osei (author): Yep—reason codes are a small fixed set (documented in docs/internal/audit-logging/authz-decision-fields.md). We only log bundle version + role IDs + the code. No statements, no permission lists, no resource attributes.
Allison Grant (review): Naming: authz_role_ids vs role_ids? I’d like the prefix for schema clarity. Also, should this be in the envelope or per-event payload?

Kevin Osei (author): Kept the authz_ prefix to avoid collisions and to make it easy for downstream parsers. Implemented at envelope level since it applies consistently across event types and keeps SIEM mappings simple.
Kaitlyn Nguyen (review): Please ensure role_ids reflect the actor’s roles at evaluation time, not a later read. Also, what about service actors (API keys) that don’t have roles?

Kevin Osei (author): The middleware captures role IDs from the request auth context before calling the handler, so it’s evaluation-time. For API keys/service accounts, role_ids is omitted (empty) and decision_reason still included; policy_version still included when available.
Jordan Lee (review): For DENY_POLICY_NOT_LOADED, do we want to treat that as an internal error rather than deny? (Concern: could mask outages.)

Kevin Osei (author): Good call. For now, the authz layer returns 503 in that condition on enforcement paths; the audit log will still record decision_reason=DENY_POLICY_NOT_LOADED with outcome=error (existing field). I updated the tests to reflect that and added a doc note.
Allison Grant (review): Please add a fixture showing the 503 case and make sure schema fixtures still validate.
Kevin Osei (author): Added fixtures/audit_authz_policy_not_loaded.json and validated via schema-validate. CI is green.
Marcus Lin (approval): Looks good. Thanks for keeping the fields minimal and machine-readable.
Kaitlyn Nguyen (approval): Approved. This unblocks the RBAC v2 audit evidence story.
Allison Grant (approval): Approved after fixture addition.
